newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN LEADS FIRST GIANT SLALOM RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN LEADS FIRST GIANT SLALOM RUN.

text.p: Switzerland's Michael von Gruenigen took a commanding lead in the first run of a World Cup giant slalom on Sunday in pursuit of his second victory of the season..
Von Gruenigen, 27, the defending giant slalom World Cup title-holder who won in December in Alta Badia, Italy, stormed down the Podkoren piste in one minute 07.21 seconds.

Austrian Siegfried Voglreiter surprised his rivals with the second fastest time of 1:07.91, seven-tenths of a second slower but well-placed to improve on his best giant slalom finish, sixth in Alta Badia last month.
Norway's Kjetil-Andre Aamodt, overall World Cup champion in 1994, was third in 1:07.99 with current overall standings leader Hans Knauss of Austria fourth in 1:08.01.
